```python
def load_target_genes_from_frame(audited: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Return one row per unique target symbol.

    Targets = `recommended_headline_flag=true` rows from t483 (any category)
    unioned with the t478 special-attention set. Deduplicates on `symbol`,
    keeping the best (lowest) `category_rank` and the union of `category`
    memberships.
    """
    selected = audited.filter(
        pl.col("recommended_headline_flag") | pl.col("symbol").is_in(SPECIAL_GENES)
    )
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for symbol_key, group in selected.group_by("symbol", maintain_order=True):
        symbol_text = str(symbol_key[0] if isinstance(symbol_key, tuple) else symbol_key)
        rows.append(
            {
                "symbol": symbol_text,
                "target_categories": ",".join(
                    sorted(set(group["category"].to_list()))
                ),
                "best_category_rank": int(group["category_rank"].min()),
                "recommended_headline_flag": bool(
                    group["recommended_headline_flag"].any()
                ),
                "special_attention_flag": symbol_text in SPECIAL_GENES,
            }
        )
    return pl.DataFrame(rows).sort("best_category_rank")


def load_target_genes(t483_path: Path) -> pl.DataFrame:
    audited = pl.read_csv(t483_path, separator="\t")
    return load_target_genes_from_frame(audited)
```

```python
def compute_attenuation(
    *,
    beta_unadj: float,
    beta_adj: float,
    unstable_threshold: float = UNSTABLE_BASELINE_THRESHOLD,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Compute attenuation diagnostics for one (gene, cell) fit."""
    if not math.isfinite(beta_unadj) or not math.isfinite(beta_adj):
        return {
            "attenuation": None,
            "sign_flip": False,
            "strengthened_after_adjustment": False,
            "unstable": True,
        }
    if abs(beta_unadj) < unstable_threshold:
        return {
            "attenuation": None,
            "sign_flip": False,
            "strengthened_after_adjustment": False,
            "unstable": True,
        }
    sign_flip = (beta_unadj > 0) != (beta_adj > 0) and beta_adj != 0.0
    attenuation = 1.0 - abs(beta_adj) / abs(beta_unadj)
    strengthened = (not sign_flip) and attenuation < 0.0
    return {
        "attenuation": float(attenuation),
        "sign_flip": bool(sign_flip),
        "strengthened_after_adjustment": bool(strengthened),
        "unstable": False,
    }
```

```python
def assign_gene_label(
    *,
    unstable: bool,
    sign_flip: bool,
    strengthened: bool,
    attenuation: float | None,
) -> str:
    """Label a gene per the design's six-rule priority order."""
    if unstable:
        return "unstable"
    if sign_flip:
        return "sign_flip"
    if strengthened:
        return "strengthened_after_adjustment"
    if attenuation is None:
        return "unstable"
    if attenuation > ATTENUATION_HIGH:
        return "8q24_mediated_or_confounded"
    if attenuation >= ATTENUATION_LOW:
        return "partial_8q24_mediation"
    return "rearrangement_specific_beyond_8q24"
```

```python
def fit_ols(
    *, y: np.ndarray, design: np.ndarray, coefficient_names: Sequence[str]
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Homoskedastic multivariate OLS with manual SE / t / p computation.

    Aborts with `ValueError` if the design is rank-deficient.
    """
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    design = np.asarray(design, dtype=float)
    n, p = design.shape
    if len(coefficient_names) != p:
        raise ValueError(
            f"coefficient_names length {len(coefficient_names)} != design ncol {p}"
        )
    rank = int(np.linalg.matrix_rank(design))
    if rank != p:
        raise ValueError(
            f"rank-deficient design: rank {rank} < expected {p}"
        )
    df_resid = n - p
    if df_resid <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"non-positive residual df: n={n}, p={p}")
    beta, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(design, y, rcond=None)
    resid = y - design @ beta
    sse = float(resid @ resid)
    mse = sse / df_resid
    xtx_inv = np.linalg.inv(design.T @ design)
    var_beta = mse * np.diag(xtx_inv)
    se = np.sqrt(np.maximum(var_beta, 0.0))
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for name, b, s in zip(coefficient_names, beta, se):
        if s > 0 and math.isfinite(s):
            t_stat = float(b) / float(s)
            p_value = float(2.0 * stats.t.sf(abs(t_stat), df_resid))
        else:
            t_stat = math.copysign(math.inf, b) if b != 0.0 else 0.0
            p_value = 0.0 if t_stat != 0.0 else 1.0
        rows.append(
            {
                "coefficient": name,
                "beta": float(b),
                "se": float(s),
                "signed_t": float(t_stat),
                "p_value": float(p_value),
                "df_resid": int(df_resid),
                "n_used": int(n),
            }
        )
    return rows
```

```python
    "none": (),
    "myc_only": ("MYC_z",),

def build_design(
    df: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    anchor_col: str,
    adjustment_set: str,
    proliferation_adjusted: bool,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Build the OLS design matrix for one model cell.

    Returns dict with keys `design` (np.ndarray of shape (n, p)) and
    `coefficient_names` (list[str]).
    """
    if adjustment_set not in ADJUSTMENT_SETS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown adjustment_set: {adjustment_set}")
    covariate_cols = list(ADJUSTMENT_SETS[adjustment_set])
    if proliferation_adjusted:
        covariate_cols = [*covariate_cols, "proliferation_z"]

    n = df.height
    columns: list[np.ndarray] = [np.ones(n, dtype=float)]
    names: list[str] = ["intercept", anchor_col]
    columns.append(df[anchor_col].to_numpy().astype(float))
    for col in covariate_cols:
        columns.append(df[col].to_numpy().astype(float))
        names.append(col)
    design = np.column_stack(columns)
    return {"design": design, "coefficient_names": names}
```

```python
def standardized_mean_difference(
    *, pos: np.ndarray, neg: np.ndarray
) -> float:
    """Cohen's d-style standardized mean difference, pooled SD."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    neg = np.asarray(neg, dtype=float)
    pos = pos[np.isfinite(pos)]
    neg = neg[np.isfinite(neg)]
    if pos.size < 2 or neg.size < 2:
        return float("nan")
    mean_diff = float(np.mean(pos) - np.mean(neg))
    var_pos = float(np.var(pos, ddof=1))
    var_neg = float(np.var(neg, ddof=1))
    pooled_sd = math.sqrt((var_pos + var_neg) / 2.0)
    if pooled_sd == 0.0 or not math.isfinite(pooled_sd):
        return float("nan")
    return mean_diff / pooled_sd
```

```python
def bh_adjust(p_values: Sequence[float | None]) -> list[float]:
    """Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment with NaN passthrough."""
    arr = np.array([float("nan") if v is None else float(v) for v in p_values], dtype=float)
    finite_mask = np.isfinite(arr)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    if finite_mask.any():
        _, padj_finite, _, _ = multipletests(arr[finite_mask], method="fdr_bh")
        out[finite_mask] = padj_finite
    return [float(v) for v in out]
```

```python
def _zscore_array(values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    arr = values.astype(float)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    if int(finite.sum()) < 2:
        return out
    sd = float(np.std(arr[finite], ddof=1))
    if sd == 0.0 or not math.isfinite(sd):
        return out
    out[finite] = (arr[finite] - float(np.mean(arr[finite]))) / sd
    return out


def load_analysis_frame(
    data_root: Path, target_symbols: Sequence[str]
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Load ground_truth + imputed labels + proliferation, return one wide frame.

    Note: the unified `myc_r` column from ground_truth is intentionally NOT
    used as a label source. The disaggregated `myc_r_pairoscope` (training
    label) and `myc_r_sv` (independent SV label) are the genomic anchors.
    """
    import sys as _sys

    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    if str(repo_root / "scripts") not in _sys.path:
        _sys.path.insert(0, str(repo_root / "scripts"))
    from stages.cytogenetics.proliferation_score import (  # noqa: E402
        compute_proliferation_score,
    )

    gt = pl.read_parquet(data_root / "cytogenetics" / "ground_truth.parquet")
    imputed = (
        pl.read_parquet(
            data_root / "cytogenetics" / "imputed" / "MMRF_cytogenetics.parquet"
        )
        .select("sample_id", "myc_r_call", "myc_r_score")
        .rename({"sample_id": "patient_id"})
    )

    # Raw-TPM scale guard (uses MYC sentinel from the gt frame)
    assert_raw_tpm_scale(gt, sentinel_gene="MYC")

    # Build long-form expression for compute_proliferation_score
    panel = list(EIGHT_Q24_PANEL) + list(target_symbols)
    panel_in_frame = [g for g in panel if g in gt.columns]
    log_expr = gt.with_columns(
        [(pl.col(g).cast(pl.Float64).log1p() / math.log(2.0)).alias(g) for g in panel_in_frame]
    )

    # Proliferation score on the original (raw TPM) frame so the helper applies its own log
    long_expr = (
        gt.select(["patient_id", *panel_in_frame])
        .unpivot(index="patient_id", variable_name="symbol", value_name="expr")
        .pivot(values="expr", index="symbol", on="patient_id")
    )
    prolif = compute_proliferation_score(long_expr, gene_col="symbol").rename(
        {"sample_id": "patient_id"}
    )

    frame = log_expr.join(imputed, on="patient_id", how="inner").join(
        prolif, on="patient_id", how="inner"
    )

    # z-score 8q24 covariates and proliferation
    z_cols: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    for col in EIGHT_Q24_PANEL:
        if col in frame.columns:
            z_cols[f"{col}_z"] = _zscore_array(frame[col].to_numpy())
    z_cols["proliferation_z"] = _zscore_array(frame["proliferation_score"].to_numpy())
    frame = frame.with_columns(
        [pl.Series(name, values) for name, values in z_cols.items()]
    )
    return frame


def expression_z_for_gene(frame: pl.DataFrame, symbol: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return z-scored log2(TPM+1) expression for one target gene."""
    if symbol not in frame.columns:
        return np.full(frame.height, np.nan, dtype=float)
    return _zscore_array(frame[symbol].to_numpy())
```

```python
class CellSpec:

HEADLINE_CELLS: tuple[CellSpec, ...] = (

    CellSpec("C_raw", "myc_only", False),
    CellSpec("C_prolif", "myc_only", True),

def _complete_case_mask(*arrays: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    if not arrays:
        raise ValueError("no arrays provided")
    mask = np.isfinite(arrays[0])
    for arr in arrays[1:]:
        mask &= np.isfinite(arr)
    return mask


def fit_one_cell(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    symbol: str,
    anchor_col: str,
    cell: CellSpec,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Fit one (gene, cell) OLS and the matching unadjusted reference.

    Returns the row that lands in `per_gene_attenuation.tsv` for this cell.
    """
    expr_z = expression_z_for_gene(frame, symbol)
    anchor = frame[anchor_col].to_numpy().astype(float)
    design_info = build_design(
        frame,
        anchor_col=anchor_col,
        adjustment_set=cell.adjustment_set,
        proliferation_adjusted=cell.proliferation_adjusted,
    )
    design = design_info["design"]
    names = design_info["coefficient_names"]

    mask = _complete_case_mask(expr_z, *(design[:, j] for j in range(design.shape[1])))
    n_used = int(mask.sum())
    base: dict[str, object] = {
        "symbol": symbol,
        "anchor": anchor_col,
        "cell_id": cell.cell_id,
        "adjustment_set": cell.adjustment_set,
        "proliferation_adjusted": bool(cell.proliferation_adjusted),
        "n_used": n_used,
    }
    if n_used <= len(names) + 2:
        base.update(
            {
                "beta_unadj_signed": None,
                "beta_adj_signed": None,
                "se_adj": None,
                "signed_t_adj": None,
                "p_value_adj": None,
                "attenuation": None,
                "sign_flip": False,
                "strengthened_after_adjustment": False,
                "unstable": True,
                "status": "too_few_samples",
            }
        )
        return base

    # Adjusted fit (this cell)
    adj_rows = fit_ols(
        y=expr_z[mask], design=design[mask], coefficient_names=names
    )
    adj_anchor_row = next(row for row in adj_rows if row["coefficient"] == anchor_col)

    # Matched unadjusted reference (same proliferation-adjustment status, no 8q24 covariates)
    unadj_design_info = build_design(
        frame,
        anchor_col=anchor_col,
        adjustment_set="none",
        proliferation_adjusted=cell.proliferation_adjusted,
    )
    unadj_design = unadj_design_info["design"]
    unadj_names = unadj_design_info["coefficient_names"]
    unadj_mask = _complete_case_mask(
        expr_z, *(unadj_design[:, j] for j in range(unadj_design.shape[1]))
    )
    unadj_rows = fit_ols(
        y=expr_z[unadj_mask],
        design=unadj_design[unadj_mask],
        coefficient_names=unadj_names,
    )
    unadj_anchor_row = next(
        row for row in unadj_rows if row["coefficient"] == anchor_col
    )

    diagnostics = compute_attenuation(
        beta_unadj=float(unadj_anchor_row["beta"]),
        beta_adj=float(adj_anchor_row["beta"]),
    )
    base.update(
        {
            "beta_unadj_signed": float(unadj_anchor_row["beta"]),
            "beta_adj_signed": float(adj_anchor_row["beta"]),
            "se_adj": float(adj_anchor_row["se"]),
            "signed_t_adj": float(adj_anchor_row["signed_t"]),
            "p_value_adj": float(adj_anchor_row["p_value"]),
            "attenuation": diagnostics["attenuation"],
            "sign_flip": diagnostics["sign_flip"],
            "strengthened_after_adjustment": diagnostics[
                "strengthened_after_adjustment"
            ],
            "unstable": diagnostics["unstable"],
            "status": "ok",
        }
    )
    return base


def run_anchor(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    target_symbols: Sequence[str],
    anchor_col: str,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for symbol in target_symbols:
        for cell in HEADLINE_CELLS:
            rows.append(
                fit_one_cell(frame, symbol=symbol, anchor_col=anchor_col, cell=cell)
            )
    return rows


def attach_bh_and_labels(
    rows: list[dict[str, object]],
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Add `padj_bh_adj` per (anchor, cell_id) group and `gene_label` for the headline cell."""
    enriched = [dict(row) for row in rows]
    groups: dict[tuple[str, str], list[int]] = {}
    for idx, row in enumerate(enriched):
        key = (str(row["anchor"]), str(row["cell_id"]))
        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(idx)
    for indices in groups.values():
        pvals = [enriched[i].get("p_value_adj") for i in indices]
        padj = bh_adjust(pvals)
        for i, p in zip(indices, padj):
            enriched[i]["padj_bh_adj"] = p
    for row in enriched:
        if row.get("cell_id") == HEADLINE_CELL_ID:
            row["gene_label"] = assign_gene_label(
                unstable=bool(row.get("unstable")),
                sign_flip=bool(row.get("sign_flip")),
                strengthened=bool(row.get("strengthened_after_adjustment")),
                attenuation=row.get("attenuation"),
            )
        else:
            row["gene_label"] = None
    return enriched
```

```python
def compute_quartile_contrast(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    target_symbols: Sequence[str],
    anchor_col: str = "myc_r_sv",
) -> tuple[pl.DataFrame, dict[str, float]]:
    """Within MYC top-quartile, fit `expr_z ~ myc_r_sv + PVT1_z + NSMCE2_z + proliferation_z`
    per gene. Returns (per-gene table, balance-diagnostic SMDs).
    """
    myc_z = frame["MYC_z"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    finite = np.isfinite(myc_z)
    if int(finite.sum()) < 4:
        raise ValueError("MYC_z has too few finite samples for quartile contrast")
    threshold = float(np.quantile(myc_z[finite], 0.75))
    in_top = finite & (myc_z >= threshold)
    sub = frame.filter(pl.Series(in_top))

    pos_mask = sub[anchor_col].to_numpy().astype(float) == 1.0
    neg_mask = sub[anchor_col].to_numpy().astype(float) == 0.0
    smds: dict[str, float] = {}
    for axis in ("MYC_z", "PVT1_z", "NSMCE2_z", "proliferation_z"):
        if axis in sub.columns:
            axis_values = sub[axis].to_numpy().astype(float)
            smds[axis] = standardized_mean_difference(
                pos=axis_values[pos_mask], neg=axis_values[neg_mask]
            )

    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for symbol in target_symbols:
        expr_z = expression_z_for_gene(sub, symbol)
        design_info = build_design(
            sub,
            anchor_col=anchor_col,
            adjustment_set="myc_pvt1",  # PVT1 only (skip MYC since restricted)
            proliferation_adjusted=True,
        )
        # Replace MYC_z column with NSMCE2_z to match the spec exactly:
        # within-quartile model = anchor + PVT1_z + NSMCE2_z + proliferation_z
        design = design_info["design"]
        names = list(design_info["coefficient_names"])
        nsmce2 = sub["NSMCE2_z"].to_numpy().astype(float)
        myc_idx = names.index("MYC_z")
        design[:, myc_idx] = nsmce2
        names[myc_idx] = "NSMCE2_z"

        mask = _complete_case_mask(
            expr_z, *(design[:, j] for j in range(design.shape[1]))
        )
        if int(mask.sum()) <= len(names) + 2:
            rows.append(
                {
                    "symbol": symbol,
                    "n_pos": int(pos_mask.sum()),
                    "n_neg": int(neg_mask.sum()),
                    "n_used": int(mask.sum()),
                    "beta_anchor": None,
                    "se_anchor": None,
                    "signed_t_anchor": None,
                    "p_value_anchor": None,
                    "status": "too_few_samples",
                }
            )
            continue
        ols_rows = fit_ols(y=expr_z[mask], design=design[mask], coefficient_names=names)
        anchor_row = next(r for r in ols_rows if r["coefficient"] == anchor_col)
        rows.append(
            {
                "symbol": symbol,
                "n_pos": int(pos_mask.sum()),
                "n_neg": int(neg_mask.sum()),
                "n_used": int(mask.sum()),
                "beta_anchor": float(anchor_row["beta"]),
                "se_anchor": float(anchor_row["se"]),
                "signed_t_anchor": float(anchor_row["signed_t"]),
                "p_value_anchor": float(anchor_row["p_value"]),
                "status": "ok",
            }
        )
    pvals = [row.get("p_value_anchor") for row in rows]
    for row, padj in zip(rows, bh_adjust(pvals)):
        row["padj_bh_anchor"] = padj
```

```python
def run_expression_derived_sensitivity(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    target_symbols: Sequence[str],
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Run the headline cell with `myc_r_call` (binary) and `myc_r_score` (continuous-z) anchors.

    These anchors are expression-derived; appendix is non-headline.
    """
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for anchor_col, transform in (("myc_r_call", "binary"), ("myc_r_score", "continuous_z")):
        if anchor_col == "myc_r_score":
            score_z = _zscore_array(frame[anchor_col].to_numpy())
            local = frame.with_columns(pl.Series("myc_r_score_z", score_z))
            anchor_for_design = "myc_r_score_z"
        else:
            local = frame
            anchor_for_design = anchor_col
        for symbol in target_symbols:
            cell = CellSpec(HEADLINE_CELL_ID, "full_8q24", True)
            row = fit_one_cell(local, symbol=symbol, anchor_col=anchor_for_design, cell=cell)
            row["anchor_kind"] = transform
            row["non_headline"] = True
            rows.append(row)
    pvals_by_anchor: dict[str, list[float | None]] = {}
    indices_by_anchor: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for idx, row in enumerate(rows):
        key = str(row["anchor"])
        pvals_by_anchor.setdefault(key, []).append(row.get("p_value_adj"))
        indices_by_anchor.setdefault(key, []).append(idx)
    for anchor, idxs in indices_by_anchor.items():
        for i, padj in zip(idxs, bh_adjust(pvals_by_anchor[anchor])):
            rows[i]["padj_bh_adj"] = padj
    return rows
```

```python
def compute_program_summary(rows: Iterable[dict[str, object]]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """One row per (anchor, cell_id) with median attenuation, IQR, and label tallies."""
    df = pl.DataFrame(list(rows))
    summaries: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for (anchor, cell_id), group in df.group_by(["anchor", "cell_id"], maintain_order=True):
        anchor_text = str(anchor[0] if isinstance(anchor, tuple) else anchor)
        cell_text = str(cell_id[0] if isinstance(cell_id, tuple) else cell_id)
        atten = (
            group["attenuation"]
            .drop_nulls()
            .to_numpy()
            .astype(float)
        )
        atten = atten[np.isfinite(atten)]
        # Labels are only set for the headline cell
        if cell_text == HEADLINE_CELL_ID:
            labels = group["gene_label"].to_list()
        else:
            labels = []
        summaries.append(
            {
                "anchor": anchor_text,
                "cell_id": cell_text,
                "n_genes": int(group.height),
                "median_attenuation": (
                    float(np.median(atten)) if atten.size else None
                ),
                "iqr_lo_attenuation": (
                    float(np.quantile(atten, 0.25)) if atten.size else None
                ),
                "iqr_hi_attenuation": (
                    float(np.quantile(atten, 0.75)) if atten.size else None
                ),
                "n_8q24_mediated_or_confounded": labels.count("8q24_mediated_or_confounded"),
                "n_partial_8q24_mediation": labels.count("partial_8q24_mediation"),
                "n_rearrangement_specific_beyond_8q24": labels.count(
                    "rearrangement_specific_beyond_8q24"
                ),
                "n_strengthened_after_adjustment": labels.count(
                    "strengthened_after_adjustment"
                ),
                "n_sign_flip": labels.count("sign_flip"),
                "n_unstable": labels.count("unstable"),
            }
        )
    return pl.DataFrame(summaries)


def derive_headline_verdict(program_summary: pl.DataFrame, *, anchor: str) -> str:
    """Map the median attenuation in the headline cell to the verdict label."""
    headline_row = program_summary.filter(
        (pl.col("anchor") == anchor) & (pl.col("cell_id") == HEADLINE_CELL_ID)
    )
    if headline_row.height == 0:
        return "unresolved_no_headline_cell"
    median = headline_row["median_attenuation"][0]
    if median is None:
        return "unresolved_all_unstable"
    if median > ATTENUATION_HIGH:
        return "8q24_mediated_or_confounded"
    if median < ATTENUATION_LOW:
        return "rearrangement_specific_beyond_8q24"
    return "partial_8q24_mediation"
```

```python
def write_outputs(

    )

        output_dir / "myc_high_quartile_contrast.tsv", separator="\t"
    )
    (output_dir / "summary.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
    )


def build_top_summary(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    target_symbols: Sequence[str],
    program_summary: pl.DataFrame,
    quartile_smds: dict[str, float],
) -> dict[str, object]:
    nan_rates = {
        col: float(frame[col].null_count() + (
            frame[col].is_nan().sum() if frame[col].dtype == pl.Float64 else 0
        )) / max(frame.height, 1)
        for col in (
            "myc_r_sv",
            "myc_r_pairoscope",
            "myc_r_call",
            "myc_r_score",
            "MYC_z",
            "PVT1_z",
            "NSMCE2_z",
            "proliferation_z",
        )
        if col in frame.columns
    }
    summary: dict[str, object] = {
        "task": "t479",
        "n_samples": frame.height,
        "n_target_genes": len(target_symbols),
        "unstable_baseline_threshold": UNSTABLE_BASELINE_THRESHOLD,
        "covariate_nan_rate": nan_rates,
        "quartile_balance_smd": quartile_smds,
        "program_summary": program_summary.to_dicts(),
        "headline_verdict_myc_r_sv": derive_headline_verdict(
            program_summary, anchor="myc_r_sv"
        ),
        "headline_verdict_myc_r_pairoscope": derive_headline_verdict(
            program_summary, anchor="myc_r_pairoscope"
        ),
    }
    return summary


def run_analysis(
    data_root: Path, output_dir: Path, t483_path: Path
) -> dict[str, object]:
    target_meta = load_target_genes(t483_path)
    target_symbols = target_meta["symbol"].to_list()
    frame = load_analysis_frame(data_root, target_symbols)

    sv_rows = attach_bh_and_labels(
        run_anchor(frame, target_symbols=target_symbols, anchor_col="myc_r_sv")
    )
    pairoscope_rows = attach_bh_and_labels(
        run_anchor(frame, target_symbols=target_symbols, anchor_col="myc_r_pairoscope")
    )
    expression_rows = run_expression_derived_sensitivity(
        frame, target_symbols=target_symbols
    )
    quartile_table, quartile_smds = compute_quartile_contrast(
        frame, target_symbols=target_symbols, anchor_col="myc_r_sv"
    )
    program_summary = compute_program_summary([*sv_rows, *pairoscope_rows])
    summary = build_top_summary(
        frame,
        target_symbols=target_symbols,
        program_summary=program_summary,
        quartile_smds=quartile_smds,
    )

    write_outputs(
        output_dir=output_dir,
        sv_rows=sv_rows,
        pairoscope_rows=pairoscope_rows,
        expression_rows=expression_rows,
        quartile_table=quartile_table,
        quartile_smds=quartile_smds,
        program_summary=program_summary,
        summary=summary,
    )
    return summary


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--data-root", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_DATA_ROOT)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR)
    parser.add_argument("--t483-path", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_T483_PATH)
    return parser.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    summary = run_analysis(args.data_root, args.output_dir, args.t483_path)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## The binding target (from pre-registration:0015, Amendment 3)

A `task:t590` run counts as **discriminating evidence** only if the realized matched-opportunity table
clears all of:

1. ≥ **12 eligible neighborhood clusters with matched within-cluster hypothesis:0002-enriched-categorical-lenses opportunities**;
2. ≥ **6 clusters with `D_c ≥ 2`** (`D_c` = `cluster_de_conf_count`);
3. ≥ **3 distinct observed `D_c` values**;
4. **`rank([1, D_c, U_c]) = 3`** with `U_c` = `FamilyHandle`-unit count, and no perfect `D_c`/`U_c`
   collinearity;
5. permutation-estimated **`power(β_min) ≥ 80%`** on that table (no-peeking; `σ_ε` from the frozen
   t594 baseline).

A within-cluster matched opportunity requires the FieldCount hypothesis:0002-enriched-categorical-lenses composition-law to be computable over
the cluster under **both** the `FamilyHandle` projection and the `CorrespondenceAssertion` projection.
Two consequences fixed by the pre-reg: **`D_c = 1` clusters yield zero confirmatory opportunities**
(so the denominator is effectively "clusters at `D_c ≥ 2`"), and **within-handle de-conflation alone
is not sufficient** — a multi-assertion handle with `< 3` `FamilyHandle` members is excluded unless it
sits in a principled sibling-neighborhood.

# t784 — entropy-dissipation / JKO breadth probe (the definite-integral register)

## Goal

Run two gradient-flow / entropy witnesses through the move-witness register pipeline to test
whether interpretation:0200's **located analytic frontier** — the multiplicative functional
equation — is the *whole* B3 obstruction, or only one of its parts. The probe's finding:
B3's analytic obstruction is **two independent registers** —

1. the **definite-integral register** (integration by parts, boundary vanishing, mass
   normalization), *newly isolated here*, and
2. the **functional-equation register** (log/exp functional equation), *located in t782* —

each with a minimal witness, and jointly the analytic content of the JKO/entropy family.

## Background

Breadth probe #1 (task:t780 → interpretation:0199) showed Cole–Hopf's transcendental
*appearance* is a **removable** localization register. Breadth probe #2 (task:t782 →
interpretation:0200) tested *irreducible* exponential content: a linear-homogeneous
exponential witness (plane wave, heat kernel) still decides under an **exponential closure**
(a 5th decidable register), but the multiplicative functional equation `exp(a+b)=exp(a)exp(b)`
is **not** a differential consequence of that closure — it is the **first genuinely-analytic
register the algebraic pipeline does not subsume**. interpretation:0200 explicitly flagged its
own scope: it demonstrated only the *multiplicative half* of B3, and noted that a fuller
entropy-dissipation witness "additionally needs a *definite-integral* oracle — Gaussian
normalization `∫exp(−x²/4νt)dx = √(4πνt)` is not even representable in the jet algebra … that
integral register is noted but not mechanized here."

This probe (task:t784) executes that test on the canonical JKO gradient-flow structure
[@JordanKinderlehrerOtto1998]: the heat equation is the Wasserstein-2 gradient flow of the
Boltzmann entropy `H[ρ]=∫ρ ln ρ`, and the Fokker–Planck equation is the gradient flow of the
free energy `F[ρ]=∫ρ ln(ρ/ρ_∞)`. The de Bruijn / entropy-dissipation identity is their
infinitesimal content.

**The subtlety that sharpens the result.** In the *bare* de Bruijn identity for the heat
equation, the `ln`'s **derivatives** are removable (`∂ₓ ln ρ = ρₓ/ρ`, the t780 localization
register). So the bare entropy dissipation needs the **definite-integral** register but **not**
the functional equation. The functional equation only re-enters when an *equilibrium*
`ρ_∞ = e^{−V}/Z` is used and the relative entropy is split `ln(ρ/ρ_∞) = ln ρ − ln ρ_∞`. This
means the two frontier registers are **independent**, each with its own isolating witness —
a sharper statement than interpretation:0200's conjectured "the pair is the complete obstruction."

## Approach

Reuse `scripts/egraph_move_spike/` end to end — no new engine. Add one probe module
`entropy_dissipation_probe.py` following the `exp_closure_probe.py` convention: plain jet /
log generators decided by `ring_decides_zero(..., interpreted_relations=(...))` (Gröbner ideal
membership), with the transcendental / integral steps supplied as **relation schemas** and
their load-bearing status established by **drop-and-recheck** (the t783 pattern). Each witness
is mechanized at **two levels**:

- a **pointwise core** — a local conservation law in the jet + log algebra that the *existing*
  decidable registers (differential, localization, ring) decide; and
- a **global level** — symbolic integrated quantities plus the frontier **schema** whose
  load-bearing status is the finding.

### Witness 1 — `entropy-dissipation` (de Bruijn, heat), isolates the definite-integral register

- **Pointwise core (decidable).** With `L = ln ρ`, entropy density `e = ρ L`, flux
  `J = ρₓ(L+1)`, the conservation law
  `∂ₜ(ρL) + ν ρₓ²/ρ − ν ∂ₓ(ρₓ L + ρₓ) = 0`
  reduces to `(L+1)·(ρₜ − ν ρₓₓ)` and decides against
  `(ρ·ρ⁻¹−1, L_x−ρₓρ⁻¹, L_t−ρₜρ⁻¹, ρₜ−ν ρₓₓ)`. Heat relation and localization are each
  load-bearing (drop either → does not decide). *No functional equation is used.*
- **Global level (the definite-integral register).** Integrating the pointwise law gives
  `Ḣ − Bnd + ν·Fish = 0` (decidable). The dissipation identity `Ḣ + ν·Fish = 0` decides **iff**
  the boundary-vanishing schema `Bnd = 0` (i.e. `∫∂ₓ(flux)dx = 0`) is supplied — the
  **definite-integral register**, not representable in the jet algebra. → **isolates the
  definite-integral register, independent of the functional equation.**

### Witness 2 — `free-energy-dissipation` (JKO Fokker–Planck), composes both registers

- **Pointwise core (decidable, needs the functional-equation schema).** With drift potential
  `V` (jet generators `V, Vₓ, Vₓₓ`), Fokker–Planck `ρₜ = ∂ₓ(ρₓ + ρVₓ)`, free-energy density
  `f = ρ·(L+V+lnZ)`, relative-Fisher density `g = ρₓ²/ρ + 2ρₓVₓ + ρVₓ²`, flux
  `J₂ = (ρₓ+ρVₓ)(L+V+lnZ+1)`, the conservation law `f_t + g − ∂ₓJ₂ = 0` decides against the FP
  relation + localization + the **functional-equation schema** `Lrat − (L+V+lnZ)` (where
  `Lrat = ln(ρ/ρ_∞)`). The FE schema is load-bearing at the **pointwise** level: it is what
  expresses the relative-entropy integrand `ρ·ln(ρ/ρ_∞)` in the jet algebra. Dropping it → does
  not decide (fails on the `Lrat` generator).
- **Global level (the definite-integral register again).** As in Witness 1: the dissipation
  identity `Ḟ + RelFish = 0` decides **iff** the boundary schema `Bnd₂ = 0` is supplied.
- **Distinctness (t783 drop-and-recheck).** The functional-equation schema (`Lrat`, pointwise)
  and the definite-integral schema (`Bnd₂`, global) are load-bearing on **different generators
  at different levels** — dropping one fails differently than dropping the other, so the two
  frontier registers are genuinely distinct, not two names for one obstruction.

Emit `entropy_dissipation_findings.json` in the same shape as the sibling `*_findings.json`
files, add `test_entropy_dissipation_probe.py` (≈12–14 tests) mirroring the probe test
conventions, and update `scripts/egraph_move_spike/README.md`.

## Inputs

## Tasks

   (`rho, rho_x, rho_t, rho_xx, rho_inv, L, L_x, L_t`) and a `@dataclass EntropyDissipationResult`
   mirroring `ExpClosureResult` (fields for `decided`, `pointwise_decides`,
   `definite_integral_register_load_bearing`, `functional_equation_load_bearing`,
   `registers_used`, `frontier_registers`, `uses_black_box_diff`, `extends_i0200`,
   `bounds_i0200`, notes).
2. **Witness 1 (`probe_entropy_dissipation`)** — build the pointwise conservation law + the
   global boundary-schema level; record the definite-integral register as load-bearing and the
   functional equation as **absent** (isolated). Include the load-bearing drop variants (drop
   heat, drop localization, drop boundary schema) that must not decide.
3. **Witness 2 (`probe_free_energy_dissipation`)** — build the drift pointwise law + global
   level; record **both** the functional-equation and definite-integral registers as
   load-bearing, and via drop-and-recheck that they act on distinct generators/levels.
4. **`cross_check`** (validation-only, not load-bearing) — confirm with `sp.diff`/`sp.simplify`
   that the real heat and Fokker–Planck densities satisfy the pointwise conservation laws and
   that the fed log-derivatives are the true derivatives (mirrors `cross_check_heat_kernel`).
5. **Emit `entropy_dissipation_findings.json` + `test_entropy_dissipation_probe.py`**
   (≈12–14 tests, incl. one per load-bearing drop and one asserting Witness 1 uses **no**
   functional equation while Witness 2 uses both), update the README, run the full spike suite.

## Decision criteria

- **Both witnesses behave as designed (predicted):** Witness 1 isolates the definite-integral
  register with no functional equation; Witness 2 composes functional-equation + definite-integral
  and the two are distinct under drop-and-recheck. → interpretation:0200's frontier is **confirmed
  and split into two independent registers**; the engine contract becomes **five decidable + two
  analytic-frontier registers**. **GO** to fold into the frontier characterization (and
  optionally into `move_oracle.py` as a second frontier constant). Verdict **[~]** — a qualified
  extension that both confirms and sharpens interpretation:0200; `sci:amends interpretation:0200`.
- **A witness fails to separate the registers** (e.g. the definite-integral drop does not
  un-decide because the functional equation silently covers it): that is itself a finding — the
  two registers are *not* independent — and would revise interpretation:0200's frontier picture.
- Either outcome is a publishable finding; no NULL-of-no-information.

## Validation

- The **definite-integral register** (boundary schema `Bnd`/`Bnd₂ = 0`) is load-bearing in both
  witnesses (drop → does not decide).
- The **functional-equation register** (`Lrat − (L+V+lnZ)`) is load-bearing in Witness 2 and
  **absent** in Witness 1 (the independence claim).
- The heat / FP relation and the localization closure are each load-bearing at the pointwise
  level (drop → does not decide).
- No `sp.diff`/`sp.simplify` is load-bearing on any decision (`uses_black_box_diff = False`);
  SymPy appears only in the non-load-bearing `cross_check`.
- Full `scripts/egraph_move_spike/__tests__` suite green after the addition.

## Out of scope

- Building the production egglog / slotted engine (question:0142) — gated on binder-aware
  representation, deferred.
- Composing the register normalizers into one canonical witness ordering (question:0144) —
  deferred; the compose half is already banked in t783, and the scoped confluence residue is a
  later follow-on.
- A completeness proof that {functional-equation, definite-integral} exhausts B3 — this probe
  shows the two registers are **necessary and independent**; sufficiency over all of B3
  (JKO-Wasserstein, entropy-of-Gibbs) stays suggested-not-proven, same honest scope as t782.
- Any change to the AKNS / exp-closure probes or their findings — this probe is additive.

## Notes on plan scope

This is a `probe`: one new module + test file reusing the existing harness, two witnesses, one
decision each (does the analytic identity separate into a decidable core plus load-bearing
frontier schemas?), expected ~1 day. It is deliberately not a `design` plan — the harness, ring
decision, and findings/test conventions already exist from t777–t783. Do not re-expand into a
full JKO-Wasserstein formalization; that is out of scope.

```python
# MM30_SCRIPT_METADATA
# task_ids: [t-prose-bundles]
# workflow: workflows/stages/app_export.smk::app_export_entity_prose_bundles
# decision_bearing: true

# MM30_SCRIPT_METADATA_END
"""Build per-gene grounded evidence bundles for entity_prose drafting (design 0041)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import yaml

BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION = "mm30.entity_prose_bundle.v1"
SCORE_METRIC = "sumz_wt_pval"
_SLUG_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+")
_WORD_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+")


def gene_universe(genes_path: Path) -> set[str]:
    genes = pl.read_parquet(genes_path)
    if "symbol" not in genes.columns:
        raise ValueError("genes table missing required column: symbol")
    return set(genes["symbol"].drop_nulls().to_list())


def _frontmatter(path: Path) -> dict:
    text = path.read_text()
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return {}
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    if end == -1:
        return {}
    return yaml.safe_load(text[3:end]) or {}


def _symbols_in(tokens: list[str], universe: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    out: set[str] = set()
    for tok in tokens:
        upper = tok.upper()
        if len(upper) >= 3 and any(c.isalpha() for c in upper) and upper in universe:
            out.add(upper)
    return out


def extract_candidates(entity_dirs: dict[str, Path], universe: set[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    roles: dict[str, str] = {}

    def admit(symbol: str, role: str) -> None:
        if role == "anchor" or symbol not in roles:
            roles[symbol] = role

    for kind, directory in entity_dirs.items():
        for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.md")):
            fm = _frontmatter(path)
            tags = [str(t) for t in (fm.get("tags") or [])]
            title = str(fm.get("title") or "")
            ident = str(fm.get("id") or path.stem)
            tag_syms = _symbols_in(tags, universe)
            slug_syms = _symbols_in(_SLUG_TOKEN.findall(ident), universe)
            # Candidates come from tags + slugs ONLY — titles are free text and would
            # weaken precision, so they never admit a candidate (design 0041 §6.1).
            candidate_syms = tag_syms | slug_syms
            # A hypothesis title may only escalate an already-admitted candidate to anchor.
            title_anchor = _symbols_in(_WORD_TOKEN.findall(title), universe) if kind == "hypothesis" else set()
            anchor_syms = (tag_syms | title_anchor) if kind == "hypothesis" else set()
            for sym in candidate_syms:
                admit(sym, "anchor" if sym in anchor_syms else "mentioned")
    return roles
```

```python
_REQUIRED_SCORE_COLUMNS = (SCORE_METRIC, "num_present", "num_missing")


def association_profile(symbol: str, score_tables: dict[str, Path]) -> list[dict]:
    entries: list[dict] = []
    for context in sorted(score_tables):
        path = score_tables[context]
        table = pl.read_parquet(path)
        missing = [c for c in ("symbol", *_REQUIRED_SCORE_COLUMNS) if c not in table.columns]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"{path.name} missing required column(s): {', '.join(missing)} ({SCORE_METRIC})")
        ranked = table.drop_nulls(SCORE_METRIC).sort([SCORE_METRIC, "symbol"])
        symbols = ranked["symbol"].to_list()
        if symbol not in symbols:
            continue
        rank = symbols.index(symbol) + 1
        row = ranked.filter(pl.col("symbol") == symbol).to_dicts()[0]
        entries.append({
            "ref": f"bundle:gene:{symbol}:association:{context}:{SCORE_METRIC}",
            "context": context,
            "source_table": f"tables/{path.name}",
            "metric": SCORE_METRIC,
            "metric_kind": "combined_pvalue",
            "directed": False,
            "value": float(row[SCORE_METRIC]),
            "rank": rank,
            "rank_direction": "ascending",
            "n_ranked": len(symbols),
            "num_present": int(row["num_present"]),
            "num_missing": int(row["num_missing"]),
        })
    return entries
```

```python
def _gene_in_tokens(symbol: str, *texts: str) -> bool:
    for text in texts:
        if symbol in {t.upper() for t in _WORD_TOKEN.findall(text or "")}:
            return True
    return False


def _body_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    text = path.read_text()
    if text.startswith("---"):
        end = text.find("\n---", 3)
        if end != -1:
            text = text[end + 4 :]
    return text.splitlines()


def _first_gene_line(symbol: str, lines: list[str], limit: int = 300) -> str | None:
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped and _gene_in_tokens(symbol, stripped):
            return stripped[:limit]
    return None


def narrative_context(
    symbol: str, entity_dirs: dict[str, Path], leads_report: Path
) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict], list[dict]]:
    membership: list[dict] = []
    interpretation_context: list[dict] = []
    for kind, directory in entity_dirs.items():
        for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.md")):
            fm = _frontmatter(path)
            ident = str(fm.get("id") or path.stem)
            title = str(fm.get("title") or "")
            tags = [str(t) for t in (fm.get("tags") or [])]
            if not (_gene_in_tokens(symbol, title, *tags) or _gene_in_tokens(symbol, *_SLUG_TOKEN.findall(ident))):
                continue
            if kind == "interpretation":
                # Bounded verbatim body line mentioning the gene grounds mechanism/direction
                # claims (falls back to the title when the gene is only in frontmatter).
                snippet = _first_gene_line(symbol, _body_lines(path)) or title
                interpretation_context.append({
                    "ref": f"bundle:gene:{symbol}:interpretation:{ident}",
                    "entity": ident, "title": title, "snippet": snippet,
                })
            else:
                role = "anchor" if kind == "hypothesis" and _gene_in_tokens(symbol, title, *tags) else "mentioned"
                membership.append({
                    "ref": f"bundle:gene:{symbol}:membership:{ident}",
                    "entity": ident, "role": role, "title": title,
                })
    lead_context: list[dict] = []
    if leads_report.exists():
        report_id = f"report:{leads_report.stem}"
        for line in leads_report.read_text().splitlines():
            if _gene_in_tokens(symbol, line):
                lead_context.append({
                    "ref": f"bundle:gene:{symbol}:lead:{report_id}",
                    "source": report_id, "snippet": line.strip(),
                })
    return membership, interpretation_context, lead_context


def build_bundle(
    genes_path: Path, score_tables: dict[str, Path],
    entity_dirs: dict[str, Path], leads_report: Path,
) -> dict:
    universe = gene_universe(genes_path)
    candidates = extract_candidates(entity_dirs, universe)
    genes: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for symbol in sorted(candidates):
        membership, interpretations, leads = narrative_context(symbol, entity_dirs, leads_report)
        genes[f"gene:{symbol}"] = {
            "symbol": symbol,
            "association_profile": association_profile(symbol, score_tables),
            "membership": membership,
            "interpretation_context": interpretations,
            "lead_context": leads,
        }
    return {
        "schema_version": BUNDLE_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "generated_from": {
            "gene_scores_tables": [f"tables/{p.name}" for _, p in sorted(score_tables.items())],
            "genes_table": f"tables/{genes_path.name}",
            "hypotheses_dir": str(entity_dirs.get("hypothesis", "")),
            "propositions_dir": str(entity_dirs.get("proposition", "")),
            "interpretations_dir": str(entity_dirs.get("interpretation", "")),
            "leads_report": str(leads_report),
        },
        "genes": genes,
    }


def collect_bundle_refs(bundle: dict) -> set[str]:
    refs: set[str] = set()
    for gene in bundle.get("genes", {}).values():
        for section in ("association_profile", "membership", "interpretation_context", "lead_context"):
            for entry in gene.get(section, []):
                if "ref" in entry:
                    refs.add(entry["ref"])
    return refs


def _score_tables(paths: list[Path]) -> dict[str, Path]:
    """Map context -> score parquet from an explicit, Snakemake-declared file list."""
    tables: dict[str, Path] = {}
    for path in paths:
        if path.name.startswith("gene_scores_") and path.name.endswith(".parquet"):
            tables[path.stem.removeprefix("gene_scores_")] = path
    return tables


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build entity_prose evidence bundles")
    parser.add_argument("--genes", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--scores", type=Path, nargs="+", required=True,
                        help="explicit gene_scores_*.parquet files (declared rule inputs)")
    parser.add_argument("--hypotheses", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--propositions", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--interpretations", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--leads", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    bundle = build_bundle(
        args.genes, _score_tables(args.scores),
        {"hypothesis": args.hypotheses, "proposition": args.propositions,
         "interpretation": args.interpretations},
        args.leads,
    )
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(bundle, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {args.out} ({len(bundle['genes'])} genes)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```markdown
# Entity Prose Authoring & Promotion

Procedure for drafting grounded `entity_prose` blocks from evidence bundles and
promoting them to the published registry. See design

## 2. Draft a block (agent step)

For gene `X`, read its entry in `entity_prose_bundles.json` and draft ONE
`project_summary` block grounded ONLY in that entry.

- Quantitative claims trace to an `association_profile` number; cite `sumz_wt_pval`
  and `num_present`.
- The score metric is an UNDIRECTED combined p-value. Do NOT assert direction,
  effect size, or outcome polarity ("worse survival") from a score. Direction/
  mechanism may appear only when traced to `membership`, `interpretation_context`,
  or `lead_context`, attributed as project claims.
- Barred breadth language when `num_present` is small.
- Inaccessible/DACO-gated facts appear only flagged as a hint.

fact's bundle `ref` verbatim (grammar: `bundle:gene:<SYM>:<association|membership|
```

# MM scATAC staging — GSE162337 (Frede 2021 [@Frede2021]) + GSE199268 (Leblay/Neri 2024 [@Neri2024])

> **For agentic workers:** Use `superpowers:executing-plans` to implement this
> plan task-by-task. One commit per task. This is the acquisition back-half of
> the t828 discovery arc — the front half (discover → re-triage → register →
> capability-fit routing) is [REDACTED]
> `entities/searches/0008-mm-scatac-chromatin-accessibility.md`.

## Goal

Stage the two real primary-MM chromatin-accessibility deposits found by t828 as
reproducible, Snakemake-owned MM30 external ingestions, flipping
`question:0062` from `covered-unstaged` → `covered-runnable` and giving
`question:0063`'s mark-discordance arm a genuine, validated scATAC substrate.

The staged product per dataset is the extracted, integrity-verified set of
**processed** chromatin-accessibility files (peaks/fragments/matrices) plus a
Frictionless `datapackage.json` — the substrate a downstream chromVAR /
motif-accessibility analysis would consume. **Staging stops at "the substrate is
present and structurally valid," not at a harmonized analysis object** (see Key
decision 3).

**Scope is acquisition + registration only.** No chromVAR, no motif scan, no
harmonized per-cell object, no HD/subtype inference. Those are downstream q0062
analysis and remain out of scope (and, for the HD arm, remain a residual t828
discovery gap).

## Background

t828 established that the chromatin-accessibility questions were pointed at a
mislabelled scRNA series (Tirier 2021 [@Tirier2021], GSE161801) and found the real substrates:

- **GSE162337 — Frede 2021 [@Frede2021]** (*Nat Cell Biol*): primary RRMM
  scATAC + bulk OmniATAC + CUT&RUN histone marks + Smart-seq scRNA, 9 patients +
  2 normal donors. Series TAR `GSE162337_RAW.tar` = **1.6 GB** (BED / BIGWIG /
  TXT). **Raw scATAC + Smart-seq reads withheld for patient privacy — processed
  files only.**
- **GSE199268 — Leblay/Neri 2024 [@Neri2024]** (*Blood*; PMID 37729611): primary CD138+
  t(11;14) MM scATAC (24 GSM). Series TAR `GSE199268_RAW.tar` = **~1.0 GB** (BED
  / H5). Raw reads in SRA (PRJNA819084). **This is the scATAC *SubSeries* of
  SuperSeries GSE199373** — the paired scRNA arm lives at the superseries level,
  not under GSE199268 (accuracy fix folded into Task 7).

Both are already registered (`entities/datasets/gse162337.md`,
`gse199268.md`), `access.verified: true`, `access.level: public` — so the
plan-pipeline **data-access gate PASSES** for both (origin external, verified,
public; §"Data-access gate" below).

## Architecture

Realizes `method:external-data-ingestion-pattern` (the t206-validated canonical
layout). The closest siblings are **`tirier_2021`** (t827 — the scRNA half of
this same saga; per-GSM download + verify + QA + datapackage) and
**`friedrich_2023`** (t823 — series-`RAW.tar` download → extract → verify →
datapackage). This plan uses the **`friedrich_2023` tar mechanics** (Key
decision 2) minus its clinical-metadata gate, plus a `tirier_2021`-style
**structural QA gate** as the honest "really runnable" check.

## Key decisions

### Key decision 1: Workflow-owned ingestion, not a bare `local_path` record
- **Chosen:** the `scripts/external/<slug>/` + `workflows/external/<slug>.smk` +
  `datapackage.json` pattern (tirier / friedrich / rade / oetjen / walker house
  style), entity gets `datapackage:` + `status: active`.
- **Rejected:** the older bare `local_path:` manual record (ledergor / ren2019).
- **Reason:** AGENTS.md requires decision-bearing data to be Snakemake-reachable,
  and every *recently* staged external deposit uses the workflow-owned pattern;
  the bare-`local_path` entries predate the convention.

### Key decision 2: Download + extract the series `RAW.tar`, not per-GSM enumeration
- **Chosen:** fetch `GSE#####_RAW.tar` once, extract, verify extracted members
  against `filelist.txt` declared sizes (friedrich mechanics).
- **Rejected:** enumerate and fetch per-GSM files individually (tirier mechanics).
- **Reason:** unlike tirier's 87 uniform per-GSM CSVs, these deposits carry
  *heterogeneous* processed file types (BED/BIGWIG/TXT; BED/H5) with multiple
  files per GSM; a single series tar captures the full processed set with less
  URL bookkeeping, and `filelist.txt` still gives per-file sizes for the G12
  integrity check.

### Key decision 3: Staging stops at a validated substrate, not a harmonized object
- **Chosen:** download → verify → **structural inventory-QA** (file-type
  histogram; assert the scATAC peak/fragment/matrix layer is present and
  non-empty; open each H5 and record cells × peaks; cross-check counts against
  the paper where cheap) → datapackage → entity `active`.
- **Rejected:** building a harmonized per-cell chromatin object / running chromVAR
  now (as tirier built a harmonized h5ad).
- **Reason:** the capability-fit lesson that *opened* t828 — do not over-credit.
  `covered-runnable` should mean "the substrate this question's decision needs is
  genuinely present and structurally sound," not "some files exist on disk" and
  not "the analysis is done." Building a harmonized object would prematurely
  commit to one chromVAR pipeline before q0062's analysis plan is written.

### Key decision 4: One shared GEO-deposit staging helper, per-dataset constants + datapackage
- **Chosen:** factor the near-identical tar-verify + inventory-QA logic into
  `scripts/external/geo_deposit/staging.py`, driven entirely by each dataset's
  `constants.py`; keep per-dataset `constants.py` + `build_data_package.py` + the
  two `.smk` files thin.
- **Rejected:** two fully self-contained dataset dirs with copy-pasted
  verify/inventory code (strict friedrich/rade house style).
- **Reason:** we are adding **two** structurally identical series-`RAW.tar` GEO
  chromatin deposits in one pass; Composition > Inheritance and DRY both favor a
  small shared, constants-parameterized helper over duplicated logic. *This is the
  one decision most worth a reviewer's eye* — if the maintainer prefers strict
  self-contained dirs, collapse `geo_deposit/staging.py` into each dataset dir
  (mechanical; no behavior change).

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset:gse162337` | external | true | public | **PASS** |

## Method gotchas to honor (from `method:external-data-ingestion-pattern`)

- **G1** — NCBI FTP: pass `wget -e robots=off`.
- **G3** — no `from __future__ import annotations` in any `script:`-invoked file
  (`build_data_package.py`).
- **G4** — `write_datapackage(meta, out_dir)` takes the **directory**.
- **G5** — `script:`-invoked files must prepend `scripts/` to `sys.path` themselves.
- **G8** — never redirect a relative `{output}` from inside a `cd` subshell;
  redirect after the subshell closes.
- **G12 / G13** — verify by declared `filelist.txt` size; in any download loop,
  catch each `wget` rc so `set -e` cannot abort mid-list.

# Stage the DLBCL cross-lineage comparator (q0151) — Wave-1 continuation

> **For agentic workers:** implementation-mode plan. One commit per task. Runs from an
> isolated worktree (`.worktrees/dlbcl-comparator-staging`) using the main checkout's
> `.venv` binaries (the uv/editable-`science` worktree footgun; see plan:0122 and
> `reference:worktree_uv_science`).

## Goal

Stage the two public DLBCL **survival** cohorts **GSE10846** (n=415, Lenz 2008 [@Lenz2008Stromal],
CHOP/R-CHOP) and **GSE87371** (n=223, LYSA) as workflow-owned external ingestions, so
`question:0151` — does the ribosome-program → survival direction *flip* between MM and
DLBCL — becomes **runnable** (`covered-reference → covered-runnable`). This is the first
real exercise of the data-catalog **transportability gate**: every dataset staged so far
(Tirier/Frede/Leblay) is primary MM (`primary_test`); DLBCL is the first non-MM
`contrast_control` entry, so the ledger's `mm_relation` / `bridge_assumption` machinery
gets its first live workout.

## Architecture

Reuses the external-deposit pattern (`scripts/external/<slug>/` + `workflows/external/<slug>.smk`
+ `datapackage.json`) established for tirier/frede/leblay, but the payload is a GEO **series
matrix** (author-normalized expression + embedded sample characteristics), not a RAW.tar of
raw files — so it needs a new, reusable series-matrix staging helper rather than the
tar/h5-oriented `geo_deposit` helper.

```
scripts/external/
  geo_series_matrix/            NEW  reusable series-matrix staging helper (constants-keyed)
    __init__.py
    staging.py                  NEW  parse | verify | qa subcommands, --dataset keyed
    build_data_package.py       NEW  script:-invoked datapackage builder
  dlbcl_gse10846/               NEW  cohort constants
    __init__.py
    constants.py
  dlbcl_gse87371/               NEW  cohort constants
    __init__.py
    constants.py
workflows/external/
  dlbcl_comparator.smk          NEW  both cohorts (download → parse → verify → qa → datapackage)
workflows/Snakefile             MODIFY  include the new .smk
entities/datasets/
  gse10846.md                   MODIFY  stub → staged (status:active + datapackage + contrast caveat)
  gse87371.md                   MODIFY  stub → staged
doc/plans/data-needs-audit.yaml MODIFY  q0151 stage_existing→(runnable); AML/q0148/q0149 classified
entities/questions/0151-*.md    MODIFY  (via CLI) link stays; add staging note
```

## Data-access gate (Step 2b)

Both cohorts: `origin: external`, `access.level: public`, GEO landing + series-matrix FTP
public, GPL570. Gate = **PASS on retrieval** (WP "download + verify" ends by setting
`access.verified: true` via `science dataset verify-access`). No credentials. Non-MM, so the
transportability sub-gate applies: `data_role: contrast_control`, `mm_relation: [dispute,
contextualize]` — a DLBCL survival result may *dispute* or *contextualize* the MM
ribosome-direction interpretation but may **not** `support` an MM-specific claim without a
recorded `bridge_assumption`. This plan authors no `support` edge.

## Key decisions

### Key decision 1: DLBCL only — AML is not a staging target
- **Chosen:** stage only the DLBCL survival cohorts for q0151.
- **Rejected:** staging the AML cohorts (GSE113160/GSE2191/GSE9476/wmu-aml/murine) that
  appear under q0148/q0149/q0105 in the coverage scan.
- **Reason:** those AML entities are uncurated GEO stubs linked only *indirectly* (not in any
  question's `datasets:` frontmatter); q0148's own body says "**No new data needed — entirely
  in-silico**" (MSigDB/Reactome signature projection onto MM30), and q0149 is already
  `status: answered` (interpretation:0156, via CTRP/GDSC). Staging AML to match the word
  "comparators" would over-credit exactly as the design (§2c, §4) warns. They are classified
  in the ledger (`not_external` / closed), not staged.

### Key decision 2: two survival cohorts, exclude GSE11318, defer GSE56315
- **Chosen:** GSE10846 + GSE87371 (both GPL570, both carry OS; the cohorts Wu2023 built its
  ribosome-direction survival claim on).
- **Rejected/deferred:** GSE11318 (no survival; array-CGH + expression redundant with
  GSE10846) — excluded. GSE56315 (normal tonsil B-cell subsets incl. plasmablast; a
  differentiation-axis **`lineage_reference`**, not a survival cohort) — deferred as a clean
  follow-on for the differentiation-score arm of q0151's "Thoughts".
- **Reason:** the flip test is a *survival-direction* test; only the two OS cohorts make it
  runnable. Bounding the first transportability-gate workout to those two keeps it clean.

### Key decision 3: series matrix (author-normalized), not RAW.tar re-normalization
- **Chosen:** download `GSE#####_series_matrix.txt.gz` → expression parquet + phenotype
  (survival) table; pure-Python parse (polars + gzip).
- **Rejected:** download RAW.tar of CEL files and re-run RMA in R.
- **Reason:** for a cross-lineage *contrast* (not a primary MM analysis joined into the
  meta-analysis) the author-normalized series matrix is the proportionate, standard substrate
  — it is what Wu2023 and most reanalyses use, needs no R/affy toolchain, and carries the
  survival characteristics inline. If a downstream analysis later needs raw CEL re-normalization
  that is a separate, heavier follow-on.

### Key decision 4: reusable `geo_series_matrix` helper, not per-cohort copy-paste
- **Chosen:** one constants-keyed `scripts/external/geo_series_matrix/` staging module + thin
  per-cohort `constants.py`, mirroring the `geo_deposit` precedent.
- **Rejected:** a bespoke DLBCL-only script.
- **Reason:** GEO bulk-expression contrasts recur in the design's roadmap (other heme,
  pan-cancer); a reusable series-matrix stager is durable infrastructure (`reusable: true`).

## Ingestion recipe (per cohort)

1. `_download_filelist` — series `filelist.txt` (for provenance/size guardrails).
2. `_download_series_matrix` — `GSE#####_series_matrix.txt.gz` (G1: `wget -e robots=off`; G13:
   per-file rc check).
3. `_parse_series_matrix` — split the `!Sample_*` metadata header from the
   `!series_matrix_table_begin … end` block → (a) `expression.parquet` (probe × sample, author
   values), (b) `phenotype.parquet` (sample × characteristics with parsed `os_time`,
   `os_status`, `treatment`, `coo` where present). Pure Python.
4. `_verify_integrity` — row/col counts match the header's `!Series_sample_count`; expression
   non-empty; **survival columns present and non-degenerate** (≥1 sample with both OS time and
   status). Writes a report, then raises on failure (G10: verdict-bearing output only after
   verdict).
5. `_qa_inventory` — expression value distribution sane (finite, plausible log-scale range);
   N samples with usable survival; COO/treatment distribution; writes `qa_report.{json,md}`.
6. `_build_data_package` — `script:`-invoked; `build_base_metadata` +
   `add_resource(expression, phenotype, verify_report, qa_report)` + `mm30.external_source`
   block (name/geo_accession/platform/doi/url/license/modality/role=contrast_control) →
   `write_datapackage`.

# Prediction-Interval Replication Gate Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans (or
> subagent-driven-development) to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox
> (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add per-gene 95% prediction intervals and a PI-excludes-null replication gate to
the standardized meta-analysis, paired with a small-k / Paule–Mandel estimator-sensitivity
guard, answering q0175 and the runnable half of q0176.

**Architecture:** Extract the duplicated DerSimonian–Laird engine into a shared
`scripts/shared/meta.py`, refactored so τ² estimation is separable from pooling; add
prediction-interval, Paule–Mandel (full RE refit), gate, and a single canonical
`RESULT_SCHEMA`. Both std-metafor scripts import it and emit the new columns. A new
Snakemake-owned audit script consumes the canonical `survival_os` table and reports
CI-vs-PI survivorship, small-k exposure, and DL↔PM agreement.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.13, polars, numpy, scipy, matplotlib, click, Snakemake 9, uv,
pytest. Run host-side (`bin/snakemake`) — these rules are pure-Python and declare no
container.

    keys: `pi_lower, pi_upper, pi_replicable, ci_replicable, tau2_pm, re_beta_pm,
    re_se_pm, pi_lower_pm, pi_upper_pm, pi_replicable_pm, small_k_flag`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Create `scripts/shared/tests/test_meta.py`:

```python
import math

import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import pytest

from shared.meta import (
    K_MIN,
    RESULT_SCHEMA,
    gate_excludes_null,
    pool_random_effects,
    prediction_interval,
    random_effects_dl,
    tau2_dersimonian_laird,
    tau2_paule_mandel,
)

# 3-study heterogeneous fixture (log-HR, SE)
LH = np.array([0.30, 0.50, 0.10], dtype=np.float64)
SE = np.array([0.10, 0.12, 0.15], dtype=np.float64)
HOMOG = (np.array([0.20, 0.20, 0.20]), np.array([0.10, 0.10, 0.10]))


def test_pi_wider_than_ci_when_tau2_positive():
    re = random_effects_dl(LH, SE)
    assert re["tau2"] > 0
    lo, hi = prediction_interval(re["re_beta"], re["re_se"], re["tau2"], k=3)
    ci_half = 1.96 * re["re_se"]
    pi_half = (hi - lo) / 2
    assert pi_half > ci_half


def test_pi_reduces_to_t_se_when_tau2_zero():
    from scipy.stats import t

    lo, hi = prediction_interval(0.4, 0.1, tau2=0.0, k=5)
    expected_half = t.ppf(0.975, df=3) * 0.1
    assert math.isclose((hi - lo) / 2, expected_half, rel_tol=1e-9)


def test_pi_nan_below_k3():
    lo, hi = prediction_interval(0.4, 0.1, 0.05, k=2)
    assert math.isnan(lo) and math.isnan(hi)


def test_pi_known_value():
    # Higgins-Thompson: beta +/- t_{k-2,.975} * sqrt(se^2 + tau2)
    from scipy.stats import t

    beta, se, tau2, k = 0.5, 0.1, 0.04, 4
    half = t.ppf(0.975, df=2) * math.sqrt(0.1**2 + 0.04)
    lo, hi = prediction_interval(beta, se, tau2, k)
    assert math.isclose(lo, beta - half, rel_tol=1e-12)
    assert math.isclose(hi, beta + half, rel_tol=1e-12)


def test_tau2_pm_zero_when_homogeneous():
    assert tau2_paule_mandel(*HOMOG) == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-8)


def test_tau2_pm_increases_with_heterogeneity():
    low = tau2_paule_mandel(np.array([0.2, 0.22, 0.19]), SE)
    high = tau2_paule_mandel(np.array([0.1, 0.9, 0.3]), SE)
    assert high > low


def test_pm_is_full_refit_not_tau2_swap():
    # PM path must re-pool: both beta AND se differ from DL when tau2 differs.
    re = random_effects_dl(LH, SE)
    tau2_pm = tau2_paule_mandel(LH, SE)
    assert not math.isclose(tau2_pm, re["tau2"], rel_tol=1e-6)
    pm = pool_random_effects(LH, SE, tau2_pm)
    assert not math.isclose(pm["beta"], re["re_beta"], rel_tol=1e-9)
```

```python
"""Shared random-effects meta-analysis engine.

Hosts the DerSimonian-Laird engine (previously duplicated across
standardized_metafor.py and standardized_metafor_all.py), a Paule-Mandel tau^2
estimator, Higgins-Thompson prediction intervals, and the replication-gate
columns. See entities/design/0043-pi-replication-gate-design.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from scipy.stats import chi2, norm, t

K_MIN: int = 8

RESULT_SCHEMA: dict[str, pl.DataType] = {
    "symbol": pl.Utf8,
    "n_datasets": pl.Int64,
    "datasets": pl.Utf8,
    "fe_beta": pl.Float64,
    "fe_se": pl.Float64,
    "fe_z": pl.Float64,
    "fe_pval": pl.Float64,
    "fe_hr": pl.Float64,
    "re_beta": pl.Float64,
    "re_se": pl.Float64,
    "re_z": pl.Float64,
    "re_pval": pl.Float64,
    "re_hr": pl.Float64,
    "tau2": pl.Float64,
    "i2": pl.Float64,
    "q": pl.Float64,
    "q_pval": pl.Float64,
    "pi_lower": pl.Float64,
    "pi_upper": pl.Float64,
    "pi_replicable": pl.Boolean,
    "ci_replicable": pl.Boolean,
    "tau2_pm": pl.Float64,
    "re_beta_pm": pl.Float64,
    "re_se_pm": pl.Float64,
    "pi_lower_pm": pl.Float64,
    "pi_upper_pm": pl.Float64,
    "pi_replicable_pm": pl.Boolean,
    "small_k_flag": pl.Boolean,
}


def fixed_effects_meta(log_hrs: np.ndarray, ses: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Fixed-effects inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis."""
    weights = 1.0 / (ses**2)
    pooled_beta = np.sum(weights * log_hrs) / np.sum(weights)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(1.0 / np.sum(weights))
    z = pooled_beta / pooled_se
    p = 2 * norm.sf(abs(z))
    return {
        "fe_beta": pooled_beta,
        "fe_se": pooled_se,
        "fe_z": z,
        "fe_pval": p,
        "fe_hr": np.exp(pooled_beta),
    }


def _cochran_q(log_hrs: np.ndarray, ses: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]:
    weights = 1.0 / (ses**2)
    beta_fe = np.sum(weights * log_hrs) / np.sum(weights)
    q = np.sum(weights * (log_hrs - beta_fe) ** 2)
    return q, weights


def tau2_dersimonian_laird(log_hrs: np.ndarray, ses: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """DerSimonian-Laird method-of-moments tau^2."""
    k = len(log_hrs)
    q, weights = _cochran_q(log_hrs, ses)
    df = k - 1
    c = np.sum(weights) - np.sum(weights**2) / np.sum(weights)
    return max(0.0, (q - df) / c) if c > 0 else 0.0


def tau2_paule_mandel(
    log_hrs: np.ndarray, ses: np.ndarray, max_iter: int = 100, tol: float = 1e-6
) -> float:
    """Paule-Mandel iterative tau^2 (root of generalized Q = k-1)."""
    k = len(log_hrs)
    if k < 2:
        return 0.0
    variances = ses**2
    tau2 = 0.0
    for _ in range(max_iter):
        w = 1.0 / (variances + tau2)
        mu = np.sum(w * log_hrs) / np.sum(w)
        resid2 = (log_hrs - mu) ** 2
        f = np.sum(w * resid2) - (k - 1)
        denom = np.sum(w**2 * resid2)
        if denom <= 0:
            break
        step = f / denom
        tau2 = max(0.0, tau2 + step)
        if abs(step) < tol:
            break
    return tau2


def pool_random_effects(log_hrs: np.ndarray, ses: np.ndarray, tau2: float) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Random-effects pooling given any tau^2 (weights = 1/(se^2 + tau2))."""
    re_weights = 1.0 / (ses**2 + tau2)
    pooled_beta = np.sum(re_weights * log_hrs) / np.sum(re_weights)
    pooled_se = np.sqrt(1.0 / np.sum(re_weights))
    z = pooled_beta / pooled_se
    p = 2 * norm.sf(abs(z))
    return {
        "beta": pooled_beta,
        "se": pooled_se,
        "z": z,
        "pval": p,
        "hr": np.exp(pooled_beta),
    }


def random_effects_dl(log_hrs: np.ndarray, ses: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
    """DerSimonian-Laird random-effects meta-analysis (contract-preserving wrapper)."""
    k = len(log_hrs)
    q, _ = _cochran_q(log_hrs, ses)
    df = k - 1
    tau2 = tau2_dersimonian_laird(log_hrs, ses)
    i2 = max(0.0, (q - df) / q) if q > 0 else 0.0
    pooled = pool_random_effects(log_hrs, ses, tau2)
    return {
        "re_beta": pooled["beta"],
        "re_se": pooled["se"],
        "re_z": pooled["z"],
        "re_pval": pooled["pval"],
        "re_hr": pooled["hr"],
        "tau2": tau2,
        "i2": i2,
        "q": q,
        "q_pval": 1 - chi2.cdf(q, df) if df > 0 else 1.0,
    }


def prediction_interval(
    beta: float, se: float, tau2: float, k: int, level: float = 0.95
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Higgins-Thompson 95% prediction interval; (nan, nan) when k < 3."""
    if k < 3:
        return (float("nan"), float("nan"))
    tcrit = t.ppf(1 - (1 - level) / 2, df=k - 2)
    half = tcrit * np.sqrt(se**2 + tau2)
    return (beta - half, beta + half)


def gate_excludes_null(lower: float, upper: float) -> bool:
    """True iff the whole interval is one-signed. NaN -> False (fail-closed)."""
    if math_isnan(lower) or math_isnan(upper):
        return False
    return bool(lower > 0) or bool(upper < 0)


def math_isnan(x: float) -> bool:
    return x != x


def replication_gate_columns(
    re_beta: float, re_se: float, tau2: float, log_hrs: np.ndarray, ses: np.ndarray, k: int
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """PI/PM/gate/small-k columns for one gene (design §3.2)."""
    pi_lower, pi_upper = prediction_interval(re_beta, re_se, tau2, k)
    ci_lower = re_beta - 1.96 * re_se
    ci_upper = re_beta + 1.96 * re_se
    tau2_pm = tau2_paule_mandel(log_hrs, ses)
    pm = pool_random_effects(log_hrs, ses, tau2_pm)
    pi_lower_pm, pi_upper_pm = prediction_interval(pm["beta"], pm["se"], tau2_pm, k)
    return {
        "pi_lower": pi_lower,
        "pi_upper": pi_upper,
        "pi_replicable": gate_excludes_null(pi_lower, pi_upper),
        "ci_replicable": gate_excludes_null(ci_lower, ci_upper),
        "tau2_pm": tau2_pm,
        "re_beta_pm": pm["beta"],
        "re_se_pm": pm["se"],
        "pi_lower_pm": pi_lower_pm,
        "pi_upper_pm": pi_upper_pm,
        "pi_replicable_pm": gate_excludes_null(pi_lower_pm, pi_upper_pm),
        "small_k_flag": bool(k < K_MIN),
    }
```

```python
"""Audit the PI replication gate on the canonical survival_os std-metafor table.

Reports CI-gate vs PI-gate survivorship, BH-FDR CI count (secondary reference),
small-k exposure, and DL<->PM PI-gate agreement. See design:0043 §3.4.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import click
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import polars as pl  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
from shared.meta import K_MIN  # noqa: E402


def _bh_fdr(pvals: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    order = np.argsort(pvals)
    ranked = pvals[order]
    n = len(pvals)
    q = ranked * n / (np.arange(n) + 1)
    q = np.minimum.accumulate(q[::-1])[::-1]
    out = np.empty(n)
    out[order] = np.clip(q, 0, 1)
    return out


def summarize_replication(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    n_genes = df.height
    fdr = _bh_fdr(df["re_pval"].to_numpy())
    n_ci_gate_fdr = int(np.sum(fdr < 0.05))
    pi = df["pi_replicable"].to_numpy()
    pm = df["pi_replicable_pm"].to_numpy()
    agreement = float(np.mean(pi == pm)) if n_genes else float("nan")
    below = df.filter(pl.col("pi_replicable") & (pl.col("n_datasets") < K_MIN)).height
    return pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "n_genes": [n_genes],
            "n_ci_gate": [int(df["ci_replicable"].sum())],
            "n_pi_gate": [int(df["pi_replicable"].sum())],
            "n_ci_gate_fdr": [n_ci_gate_fdr],
            "n_pi_gate_below_kmin": [below],
            "dl_pm_agreement": [agreement],
        }
    )


def _figure(df: pl.DataFrame, path: Path) -> None:
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.5))
    half = (df["pi_upper"].to_numpy() - df["pi_lower"].to_numpy()) / 2
    ax1.scatter(df["n_datasets"].to_numpy(), half, s=6, alpha=0.3)
    ax1.axvline(K_MIN, color="crimson", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"K_MIN={K_MIN}")
    ax1.set(xlabel="k (datasets)", ylabel="PI half-width", title="PI width vs k")
    ax1.legend()
    counts = [
        df.height,
        int(df["ci_replicable"].sum()),
        int(df["pi_replicable"].sum()),
    ]
    ax2.bar(["all", "CI gate", "PI gate"], counts, color=["#bbb", "#4c78a8", "#e45756"])
    ax2.set(ylabel="genes", title="CI-gate vs PI-gate survivorship")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


@click.command()
@click.option("--input", "input_path", type=click.Path(path_type=Path), required=True)
@click.option("--output-dir", type=click.Path(path_type=Path), required=True)
def main(input_path: Path, output_dir: Path) -> None:
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    df = pl.read_csv(input_path, separator="\t")
    summary = summarize_replication(df)
    summary.write_csv(output_dir / "pi_replication_summary.tsv", separator="\t")
    _figure(df, output_dir / "pi_replication_audit.png")
    print(summary)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
